title: A chair is drawn: cis or trans, is it the most stable, and if not draw the one that is
asks: A disubstituted cyclohexane is drawn as a chair. Say cis or trans, say whether it is the most stable conformation, and if not draw the most stable one.

know.h: A chair has two kinds of positions. The six axial bonds are vertical. The six equatorial bonds point out around the middle of the ring, each one parallel to the ring bonds one bond away.

Axial bonds alternate up, down, up, down around the ring. On every carbon the equatorial bond points to the opposite face from the axial bond: where the axial bond is up, the equatorial bond is the down one.
cis means both groups on the same face of the ring (both up or both down). trans means opposite faces. Up and down are about faces, not about axial and equatorial.
1,2 pattern: one axial and one equatorial is cis. Two equatorial, or two axial, is trans. Two equatorial neighbours look as if they point the same way, but they are trans.
1,3 pattern (the reverse of 1,2): two equatorial, or two axial, is cis. One axial and one equatorial is trans.
1,4 pattern (the same as 1,2): one axial and one equatorial is cis. Two equatorial, or two axial, is trans.
The ring flip turns every axial group equatorial and every equatorial group axial. Up stays up and down stays down, so cis stays cis and trans stays trans.
Axial groups cost energy: an axial group has two gauche interactions with the ring. An equatorial group has none.

The numbers to know (cost of an axial group, kcal/mol, and K): methyl 1.74 (19.5); ethyl 1.79 (21.2); propyl 2.21 (43.4); isopropyl 2.61 (86.0); tert-butyl 5.5 (11,916). The larger the group, the more it costs.
The most stable chair has the most groups equatorial. If one group must be axial, the larger group goes equatorial.

Size here means crowding near the ring, not the size of the atom. Halogens, including iodine, and OH cost less when axial than any alkyl group, because a single atom on a long bond stays clear of the ring. COOH and {{NH2}} cost a little less than methyl.

know.h: Skill: be able to redraw a chair after the ring flip, with each group on the same carbon and the same face, and with no wedges or dashes.

method: For each group, decide whether its bond is vertical (axial) or points outward (equatorial).
For each group, decide whether it is up or down: an axial group points straight up or down, and an equatorial group points to the face opposite the axial bond on its carbon.
Same face is cis, opposite faces is trans. Check against the pattern for 1,2, 1,3 or 1,4.
Picture the ring flip: every axial group becomes equatorial and the reverse.
Compare the two chairs: both equatorial beats everything, and when one group must be axial the larger group should be equatorial.
If the drawn chair is not the better one, draw the flipped chair with each group on the same carbon and the same face.

pitfalls.h: Calling two equatorial neighbours cis because both seem to point sideways. They are trans.
Using the 1,2 pattern for a 1,3 pair. At 1,3 two equatorial groups are cis.
Changing cis to trans when drawing the ring flip. The flip never changes up and down.
Putting the group with the biggest atom equatorial. Iodine or bromine costs less when axial than methyl does.
Saying a chair with one axial group cannot be the most stable. For a cis-1,2, trans-1,3 or cis-1,4 pair one group is always axial.
